feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence so far: in iteration 0 (baseline, 60 trials) every run went off track after about one line loss, with max_error at 0.061 to 0.063 m and steering oscillation low (0.11 to 0.15). In iteration 1, widening the sensors to ±0.045 m cut oval line-loss events from 1.05 to 0.55, so sensing reach is real. But s-bend and slalom still lost the line once per run (1.0) with max_error at 0.063 to 0.068 m, and steering oscillation rose to about 0.16. Oval progress fell from 0.175 to 0.121. The robot reacts more without recovering before the 0.06 m limit, which points to turn authority (yaw inertia and wheel track) as the constraint on those tracks. Body width cannot widen the limit, which stays at 0.06 m. I kept the iteration 1 controller unchanged so your geometry changes are tested cleanly. Use the next race as follows. If s-bend and slalom line losses fall to 0 and max_error stays below about 0.055 m, keep the mass change and check oval progress. If line losses stay at 1 with max_error near 0.06 m, the turn-authority lever is still the constraint, so narrow wheel_track. If the robot finishes but progress is low, the fix belongs in the controller speed, not the geometry.
requested_changes: If the mass 0.6 kg run still shows line_loss_events of 1 on s-bend and slalom with max_error at or above 0.06 m: set wheel_track to 0.09 m (from 0.10 m), keeping mass 0.6 kg and the ±0.045 m sensor span. Iteration 1 showed that the sensor widening alone does not fix s-bend and slalom, and narrowing the track is the remaining untested turn-authority lever.

If line losses are gone but max_error stays at 0.05 m or more on the s-bend or slalom: widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.054 with 0.027 m steps, keeping sensor_size 0.012 m. Iteration 0 showed the array reached only about ±0.036 m, and iteration 1 showed ±0.045 m helped oval line losses, so more reach may still help.

If the 0.6 kg run is kept but oval progress stays near 0.12 with no line losses: keep the geometry as it is and pass the shortfall to the controller (higher base_speed). Iteration 1 showed oval progress fell from 0.175 to 0.121, which the geometry changes alone do not explain.
